name: Build a Calculator with React & Tailwind CSS
description: A complete hands-on tutorial to build a modern calculator web app from scratch using React and Tailwind CSS — covering setup, components, state management, event handling, styling, and deployment.
whatYouLearn: Set up a React + Tailwind project from scratch
Understand React components, props, and state
Handle user input and events for calculator buttons
Implement dynamic display and mathematical operations
Apply modern responsive styling using Tailwind CSS
Organize code with modular structure and reusable components
Build and deploy the app for production
prerequisites: Basic understanding of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Comfortable using a terminal or code editor (VS Code)

exercises.title: Environment Setup & Project Initialization
exercises.description: Set up your React development environment and initialize a new React + Tailwind CSS project.
exercises.theory: React apps are built using Node.js and npm. Tailwind CSS provides utility-first CSS classes for fast UI building. We'll use Vite for faster React setup.
exercises.objective: Initialize a new React app using Vite and integrate Tailwind CSS.
exercises.initialCode:
npm create vite@latest react-calculator --template react
cd react-calculator
npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
npx tailwindcss init -p
hints: Use Vite instead of CRA for faster builds

exercises.title: Creating the App Structure
exercises.description: Set up the base layout and component structure for the calculator.
exercises.theory: React uses components to break UI into reusable parts. We'll create components for Display and Buttons inside an App container.
exercises.objective: Create App.jsx with Display and Button components organized inside a Calculator container.

exercises.title: Handling Button Clicks & State Management
exercises.description: Make the calculator interactive using React useState hook to manage display value.
exercises.theory: React’s `useState` lets you store and update data in functional components. We'll track the current input and result dynamically.
exercises.objective: Implement logic to update display when buttons are clicked.
hints: Use eval() only for demo; real apps should use math parsers

exercises.title: Improving UI and Adding Responsive Design
exercises.description: Enhance the calculator design using Tailwind utilities and make it responsive for mobile and desktop.
exercises.theory: Tailwind classes allow responsive design by prefixing breakpoints like sm:, md:, lg:. We’ll improve spacing, typography, and colors.
exercises.objective: Refine calculator look with consistent button colors, spacing, and mobile responsiveness.
exercises.solutionCode: // src/App.jsx
hints: Try gradient backgrounds and shadows for modern feel

exercises.title: Refactoring & Component Optimization
exercises.description: Split logic into smaller functions and improve maintainability by separating the display logic and operator handling.
exercises.theory: Cleaner code ensures scalability. We'll move calculation logic to a separate helper and add keyboard input support.
exercises.objective: Create a `calculate.js` helper for cleaner code and optionally add keyboard event handling.

exercises.title: Deployment
exercises.description: Build the final calculator app for production and deploy it to Vercel or Netlify.
exercises.theory: Vite builds static assets for production. Hosting services like Vercel automatically detect frameworks and deploy apps instantly.
exercises.objective: Build production version and deploy it online.
exercises.solutionCode:
npm run build
# creates /dist folder
# push to GitHub, then deploy via Vercel CLI or website
npm install -g vercel
vercel
hints: Make sure 'vite.config.js' has correct base path if deploying in subfolder
